content.text:
I found and fixed three bugs in `src/range-tree.js`. `node --test` now passes, and a randomized comparison against a plain array also passed: 3,000 random trees of up to 40 elements, each with 200 mixed operations covering every method.

**Bugs fixed:**
1. **Wrong sums after assign → add → assign (the main cause).** Assigning a value to a section of the tree didn't clear an addition that was still waiting to be passed down. When the tree later passed its updates down, it applied the new assignment and then the old addition again. Your visible test failed this way. I fixed it by clearing the waiting addition in `_applyAssignment`, so "assignment before addition" holds.
2. **Wrong maximum when all values are negative.** `_max` started from `0` instead of `-Infinity`, so `max()` returned `0` if every value in the range was negative.
3. **Wrong threshold-search results.** `_first` (used by `firstAtLeast`) looked at the lower parts of the tree without first passing down waiting updates. So after a range update it searched old maxima and returned wrong indices or `-1`.

All three fixes are small edits to the existing structure, so the API, error handling, empty-range behaviour, the CommonJS export, and the O(log n) / O(n) costs are unchanged. I deleted the randomized check after it passed, since I couldn't add tests under `test/`. It would be worth adding a check like it to the test suite, because the existing test only covers the first bug.

One limit: the fuzz check used whole numbers only. With fractional values, two pending additions are combined before they're applied, so the last digit of a result can differ slightly from adding them one at a time. Any tree that delays updates this way behaves like that, and your source comment allows ordinary JS number arithmetic.
